title: Workspace-canonical-first: lossy as-casts in query pagination (i64→usize, u64→usize) — jmap-mail-server canonical, propagate to 7 siblings
description:
Workspace-wide pattern: every extension-server MemoryBackend's `query_objects` (and related pagination call sites) uses bare `as` casts for the i64 position → usize and u64 limit → usize conversions required by RFC 8620 §5.5 pagination. These are flagged by clippy::cast_possible_truncation (32-bit targets) and clippy::cast_sign_loss (positive i64 → usize). On 64-bit targets the casts are correct-by-platform; on 32-bit targets they silently truncate.

Site counts (cargo grep, 2026-05-15):
- jmap-mail-server (CANONICAL): 11 sites across src/{memory.rs, submission.rs, sieve.rs, mailbox.rs, email.rs}.
- jmap-metadata-server: 4 sites in src/memory.rs (per bd:JMAP-826m.45).
- Other 6 extension-server siblings: unaudited; expected ~4-10 sites each.

Approach options:
(a) Single `fn clamp_position(position: i64, len: usize) -> usize` helper + `fn limit_or_max(limit: Option<u64>) -> usize` helper in jmap-server (foundation), exported, used by all 8 extension MemoryBackends. Each helper does usize::try_from + saturating fallback for 32-bit targets and documents the policy at one site.
(b) Per-crate inline #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)] + // SAFETY: comment on every cast site, justifying the 64-bit-target assumption. Verbose.
(c) Per-crate inline usize::try_from + saturating fallback (no helper extraction). Idiomatic but ~5x the code for the same correctness.

Recommendation: (a). RFC 8620 §5.5 pagination clamp semantics are identical across every JMAP /query method; centralising the policy in jmap-server makes the implementation correct on 32-bit targets, documents the clamp rule at one site, and prevents copy-paste drift. The helpers belong on the foundation crate so consumer-implemented backends (the kit's actual audience) get them too.

Per the workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template propagation rule, this MUST start with the foundation helper + jmap-mail-server adoption, then propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings in the same pass.

Discovered while triaging bd:JMAP-826m.45; closing that sibling-scoped bead in favor of this workspace-scoped one.
